the following issues: (1) the modelling of the actors and their competences, (2) the definition of a process for the capitalisation of the experience feedback, (3) the integration of the process into the technical processes of the company.
the development of a competence approach in the experience feedback process, which aims at capitalising the know-how and the experience of the actors in a company.

a competence approach in an experience feedback process is a way to improve the efficiency and acceptibility of the process and the involvement of the actors in their own work.

the EF process can be seen as a knowledge management process that aims at transforming tacit knowledge of the actors in explicit knowledge, and at capitalising the know-how and experience of the company.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the competence approach is a powerful tool for the EF process.
the competence approach is a good way to increase the acceptability and the efficiency of a knowledge management system, especially when it is based on the human resources.
the EF system is not a simple tool for data management but also a tool for knowledge management, which can be used to improve the knowledge of the company.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the EF system can be improved by taking into account a more complete representation of the knowledge and skills of the users, and by integrating the concept of “competences” in the design of the system.

a competence approach is a good way for designing a system that is both efficient and accepted by the users, and that it can be used to increase the involvement of the actors in the technical processes.
